title: Reference with singular personal pronouns
summary: Use minä for the speaker, sinä for one informal listener, and hän for one person being discussed.
objectives: Use minä for the speaker, sinä for one informal listener, and hän for one person being discussed.

sections.title: Follow the person’s role
paragraphs: Minä refers to the person speaking. Sinä addresses one listener informally. Hän refers to one person being discussed.
Hän does not mark gender: it can mean “he” or “she”. A change of speaker can change which pronoun fits the same person.

steps: The speaker addresses one person directly.
The reference is one person being discussed.

commonMistakes: Choose the pronoun from the person’s role in the conversation.
Do not force an English gender distinction onto hän.

practiceExercises.prompt: Optional practice: Which pronoun fits one person whose gender is not stated?
practiceExercises.explanation: Hän refers to one person and does not mark that person as male or female.
